Māius , i, m. Maia, usually mensis Maius,
I.the month of May: “Cincius mensem (Maium nominatum putat a Maia, quam Vulcani dicit uxorem,” Macr. S. 1, 12, 18 : “(mensis) tertius a majoribus Maius,” Varr. L. L. 6, 4, 34 ; Cic. Phil. 2, 39, 100; Ov. F. 5, 490; “also simply Maius,” Ov. F. 5, 185 .—As adj.: “Kalendae Maiae,” Cic. Fam. 4, 2, 1 ; Ov. F. 4, 947: “Idus Maiae,” Cic. Att. 3, 8, 2 ; Prop. 4 (5), 5, 36.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
